id_and_class.summary: David Builes argues that idealism is true as a matter of metaphysical necessity: in every possible world, every fundamental entity is conscious and every fundamental property is phenomenal. Only one world is fundamental; all other possible worlds exist as thoughts in the mind of a divine being or a similar ideal observer.
id_and_class.core_identity_tagline: Necessary Idealism, Possible Worlds as Divine Thoughts

conceptual_ground.explanatory_identity_claim: Consciousness is the fundamental character of reality: every fundamental property is a phenomenal property, one that specifies what it is like to be something, and this holds necessarily.
conceptual_ground.emergence_type: Not applicable (phenomenal properties are the fundamental properties, in every possible world)
conceptual_ground.subjectivity_and_intentionality: Intentionality does heavy metaphysical work: non-actual possible worlds are intentional objects, existing because a divine mind represents them in precise, structured detail.
conceptual_ground.qualia_account: Phenomenal properties, which specify what it is like to be something, are the fundamental properties of reality.
conceptual_ground.ontological_commitments: One fundamental, ungrounded actual world; conscious fundamental entities with phenomenal properties; a divine being or structurally similar ideal observer whose thoughts ground all other possible worlds.
conceptual_ground.epistemic_access: Builes argues that Modal Idealism protects our knowledge of our own conscious states against influential ‘debunking’ arguments.
conceptual_ground.constituents_and_structure: A two-tier ontology: the actual world exists fundamentally, while the existence of every other possible world is grounded in the mental activity of the divine mind.

mechanism_and_dynamics.scope_of_consciousness: The fundamental nature of reality and the nature of possibility and necessity.
mechanism_and_dynamics.distinctive_mechanism_or_principle: Possible worlds are reinterpreted as divine thoughts, combining idealism with a form of modal realism in which all possible worlds exist but only one is concrete and fundamental.
mechanism_and_dynamics.location_and_distribution: Consciousness is present in every fundamental entity, and the full space of possibilities lives in one divine mind.
mechanism_and_dynamics.causation_and_functional_role: Builes appeals to the Eleatic Principle, that every concrete object necessarily has causal powers, as support for Modal Idealism.
mechanism_and_dynamics.information_flow_or_representation: Modal truths are truths about what the divine mind represents, so modality becomes a matter of divine cognition or will.
core_claims_and_evidence: If some possible fundamental properties are phenomenal, denying Modal Idealism leads to implausible brute necessities.
Those who accept the Eleatic Principle should accept Modal Idealism.
Modal Idealism secures knowledge of our own conscious states against debunking arguments.
The view is theoretically fruitful, unifying modal metaphysics and philosophy of mind and making progress on other metaphysical debates.
mechanism_and_dynamics.basis_of_belief_or_evidence_type: Philosophical: a priori argument in metaphysics and epistemology.

empirics_and_critiques.ontological_coherence: Builes claims parsimony, since only one world is fundamental while other worlds are intentional objects. The price is a divine being, or something structurally like one, rich enough to represent every possible world.

meaning_and_purpose.rationale: Since all possibilities exist as thoughts of a divine mind, the view is compatible with theism and grounds modality in divine cognition or will.

related_theories.name: Leslie's Consciousness Inside an Infinite Mind
